accepted.s: Who founded Bengal Chemicals during the Swadeshi Movement?
accepted.x: Bengal Chemicals was founded by Acharya P.C. Ray as a Swadeshi enterprise.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–enterprise association and distinguish it from leaders of the movement.
accepted.sec: Swadeshi enterprises → founder

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Banga Lakshmi Cotton Mills was established in 1906. Bank of India was established in 1906, Indian Bank in 1907, and the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company was associated with Tuticorin in 1906.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the year and location attached to each enterprise.
accepted.sec: Swadeshi enterprises → founder

accepted.s: The Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company was associated with which of the following persons and places?
accepted.x: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai established the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company at Tuticorin in 1906.
accepted.tq: Link the entrepreneur with both the enterprise and its regional centre.
accepted.sec: Swadeshi enterprises → founder

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Swadeshi enterprises:
1. Bank of India was established in 1906.
2. Indian Bank was established in 1907.
3. Mohini Mills formed part of the Swadeshi industrial initiative.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Bank of India dates to 1906, Indian Bank to 1907, and Mohini Mills is identified with the Swadeshi enterprise movement.
accepted.tq: Check each enterprise independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Swadeshi enterprises → founder

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in the context of Andhra Swadeshi enterprise?
o: Textile unit at Vijayawada — Guneswara Rao
accepted.x: Guneswara Rao was associated with the Godavari Swadeshi Stores. Munagala Raja established the textile unit at Vijayawada.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–enterprise trap by separating similar Andhra names and institutions.
accepted.sec: Swadeshi enterprises → founder

accepted.s: The textile unit established by Munagala Raja at Vijayawada in June 1906 was significant because it was:
o: the first handloom centre established after 1911
the first such unit in the Madras Presidency
the first national college in the Madras Presidency
the first Swadeshi bank in Andhra
accepted.x: Munagala Raja’s textile unit at Vijayawada, established in June 1906, was the first of its kind in the Madras Presidency.
accepted.tq: Identify the significance attached to a precise date, place and institution.
accepted.sec: Swadeshi enterprises → founder

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of trainees and industrial skills is correctly matched?
o: Malladi Venkata Subbarao — pencils; S. Ramarao — glass and clocks
Malladi Venkata Subbarao — glass and clocks; S. Ramarao — pencils
Malladi Venkata Subbarao — textiles; S. Ramarao — shipbuilding
Malladi Venkata Subbarao — chemicals; S. Ramarao — printing
accepted.x: Malladi Venkata Subbarao trained in pencil production, while S. Ramarao trained in glass and clock manufacture; both were sent to Japan for industrial training.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure skill–person pair and eliminate the reversed combination.
accepted.sec: Swadeshi enterprises → founder

accepted.s: Who was the first principal of Bengal National College?
accepted.x: Aurobindo Ghosh served as the first principal of Bengal National College.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an institutional office from general political leadership.
accepted.sec: Swadeshi enterprises → founder

accepted.s: Which of the following was established in Madras in 1906 in connection with the Swadeshi economic programme?
o: National Council of Education and Swadesh Bandhab Samiti
Bengal National College and Indian Society of Oriental Art
Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company and Bank of India
accepted.x: The Industrial Association and Swadeshi League were established in Madras in 1906.
accepted.tq: Match the organisations with their correct regional setting and year.
accepted.sec: Swadeshi enterprises → founder

accepted.s: Who wrote the song ‘Amar Sonar Bangla’, which later became the national anthem of Bangladesh?
accepted.x: Rabindranath Tagore wrote ‘Amar Sonar Bangla’, which later became Bangladesh’s national anthem.
accepted.tq: Separate the two Tagore-associated cultural contributions by matching the work with its creator.
accepted.sec: Impact on art, literature and science

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote ‘Bande Mataram’, which became the anthem of the Swadeshi movement. ‘Desher Katha’ was written by S.G. Deuskar.
accepted.tq: Use the author–work trap involving closely associated nationalist writers.
accepted.sec: Impact on art, literature and science

accepted.s: ‘Desher Katha’ was written by S.G. Deuskar primarily to warn Indians against:
o: the use of Indian languages in administration
the decline of Sanskrit education under the Mughals
the division of Bengal into linguistic provinces
the British ‘hypnotic conquest of the mind’
accepted.x: S.G. Deuskar’s ‘Desher Katha’ warned against the British ‘hypnotic conquest of the mind’.
accepted.tq: Read the distinctive phrase as the identifying clue for the work.
accepted.sec: Impact on art, literature and science

accepted.s: Abanindranath Tagore’s painting of Bharat Mata was associated with which development in Indian art?
o: The exclusive revival of Mughal court portraiture
A nationalist art movement that broke with Victorian naturalism
The beginning of European abstract expressionism in India
A complete adoption of Victorian naturalism
accepted.x: Abanindranath Tagore’s Bharat Mata represented nationalist art and marked a break with Victorian naturalism.
accepted.tq: Connect the artwork with the artistic tendency it represented rather than with the artist’s family identity.
accepted.sec: Impact on art, literature and science

accepted.s:
Which of the following were associated with Indian scientific achievement during the Swadeshi period?
1. J.C. Bose
2. P.C. Ray
3. Nandalal Bose
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: J.C. Bose and P.C. Ray represented Indian scientific achievement. Nandalal Bose was associated with nationalist art.
accepted.tq: Separate science personalities from the artist appearing in the same cultural context.
accepted.sec: Impact on art, literature and science

accepted.s: Who was described as the ‘First Telugu national poet’?
accepted.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham was described as the ‘First Telugu national poet’.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive title to identify the correct Telugu literary figure.
accepted.sec: Impact on art, literature and science

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Hindu Desa Daridryam — Attili Suryanarayana Rao
Jatiya Nataka Rangam — Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham
Amar Sonar Bangla — Dasu Narayana Rao
accepted.x: ‘Hindu Desa Daridryam’ was associated with Attili Suryanarayana Rao. Dasu Narayana Rao was associated with the theatre work ‘Jatiya Nataka Rangam’.
accepted.tq: Begin with the sure author–title pair and reject swapped literary associations.
accepted.sec: Impact on art, literature and science

accepted.s: Which event occurred on 7 August 1905?
o: The partition of Bengal was annulled and the capital shifted to Delhi
The partition of Bengal formally took effect as a day of mourning
The boycott resolution was passed at Calcutta Town Hall and Swadeshi was formally proclaimed
The National Council of Education was established
accepted.x: On 7 August 1905, the boycott resolution was passed at Calcutta Town Hall and Swadeshi was formally proclaimed.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the formal proclamation date from the later date on which the partition took effect.
accepted.sec: Chronology - partition to annulment, Handloom Day

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. National Council of Education was established
B. Partition of Bengal took effect
C. Boycott resolution at Calcutta Town Hall
D. Partition of Bengal was annulled
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The sequence is 7 August 1905, 16 October 1905, 15 August 1906 and 12 December 1911.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the two 1905 events correctly.
accepted.sec: Chronology - partition to annulment, Handloom Day

accepted.s: The partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October 1905, which was observed as:
o: a day of mourning, Raksha Bandhan and a Swadeshi vow
the day of the Muslim League’s formation at Dacca
the day of the annulment of partition and the transfer of the capital
the day of the Surat Split and a national education conference
accepted.x: 16 October 1905 was marked by mourning, Raksha Bandhan observances and a vow to follow Swadeshi.
accepted.tq: Associate the date with its cluster of observances rather than with the announcement date.
accepted.sec: Chronology - partition to annulment, Handloom Day

accepted.s: The National Council of Education was established on:
accepted.x: The National Council of Education was established on 15 August 1906 and later became associated with Jadavpur University.
accepted.tq: Use the middle-date trap among the closely spaced Swadeshi milestones.
accepted.sec: Chronology - partition to annulment, Handloom Day

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the events of December 1906?
o: The National Council of Education was established and Home Rule Leagues began
The Surat Split occurred and Tilak was sent to Mandalay
The partition took effect and the Swadeshi vow was taken
The Muslim League was formed at Dacca and the Calcutta Congress adopted Swaraj
accepted.x: In December 1906, the Muslim League was formed at Dacca and the Calcutta Congress under Dadabhai Naoroji adopted Swaraj.
accepted.tq: Pair events sharing the same month while rejecting events from neighbouring years.
accepted.sec: Chronology - partition to annulment, Handloom Day

accepted.s: The partition of Bengal was annulled on 12 December 1911. Which other decision accompanied this step?
o: The capital was shifted from Delhi to Calcutta
The National Council of Education was dissolved
The capital of British India was shifted to Delhi
accepted.x: The annulment of the partition was accompanied by the transfer of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi.
accepted.tq: Link a political reversal with the administrative decision announced alongside it.
accepted.sec: Chronology - partition to annulment, Handloom Day

accepted.s: National Handloom Day has been observed on 7 August since:
accepted.x: National Handloom Day has been observed on 7 August since 2015, commemorating the Swadeshi proclamation at Calcutta Town Hall.
accepted.tq: Separate the historical date commemorated from the modern year in which the observance began.
accepted.sec: Chronology - partition to annulment, Handloom Day

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a principal target of the boycott programme during the Swadeshi Movement?
accepted.x: The boycott targeted foreign cloth, salt and sugar; indigenous handloom products were encouraged through the Swadeshi programme.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the central boycott–Swadeshi distinction.
accepted.sec: Techniques and programme - boycott, national education, samitis, Town Hall, Calcutta 1906

accepted.s: The Swadesh Bandhab Samiti was associated with which person and place?
accepted.x: The Swadesh Bandhab Samiti was led by Ashwini Kumar Dutt in Barisal.
accepted.tq: Use the organisation–leader–region association to distinguish Bengal samitis from other regional initiatives.
accepted.sec: Techniques and programme - boycott, national education, samitis, Town Hall, Calcutta 1906

accepted.s: Which of the following activities was associated with the Swadesh Bandhab Samiti?
o: Separate electorates, legislative councils and official recruitment
Naval training, foreign trade and railway construction
Only petitions to the Viceroy without social mobilisation
Magic-lantern demonstrations, social work and arbitration courts
accepted.x: The Swadesh Bandhab Samiti used magic-lantern demonstrations, social work and arbitration courts for mobilisation.
accepted.tq: Identify the practical activities of a samiti rather than its broad political objective.
accepted.sec: Techniques and programme - boycott, national education, samitis, Town Hall, Calcutta 1906

accepted.s:
Which of the following formed part of the mass mobilisation methods of the Swadeshi Movement?
1. Jatras and folk songs
2. Melas and volunteer corps
3. Physical-training clubs, akharas and lathi clubs
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Jatras, folk songs, melas, volunteer corps and physical-training institutions such as akharas and lathi clubs were all used for mobilisation.
accepted.tq: Treat each listed mobilisation method as an independent statement before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Techniques and programme - boycott, national education, samitis, Town Hall, Calcutta 1906

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the four resolutions of the Calcutta Congress of 1906?
accepted.x: The four resolutions were Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education. Separate electorates were connected with the Morley–Minto Reforms of 1909.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the constitutional measure that belongs to a later development, not the 1906 programme.
accepted.sec: Techniques and programme - boycott, national education, samitis, Town Hall, Calcutta 1906

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the transition in leadership during the Swadeshi Movement?
o: Leadership remained exclusively with the Moderates until 1911
Leadership passed from the Extremists to the Moderates in 1905
Leadership passed from the Moderates to the Extremists in 1906
Leadership passed directly from the Congress to the Muslim League in 1906
accepted.x: The leadership of the movement passed from the Moderates to the Extremists in 1906.
accepted.tq: Use the date and direction of transfer to avoid reversing the Moderate–Extremist relationship.
accepted.sec: Techniques and programme - boycott, national education, samitis, Town Hall, Calcutta 1906

accepted.s: S.N. Banerjee and A.M. Bose together raised approximately what amount for the Swadeshi cause?
accepted.x: S.N. Banerjee and A.M. Bose raised Rs 50,000 for the Swadeshi cause.
accepted.tq: Check the place value carefully among similarly structured monetary options.
accepted.sec: Techniques and programme - boycott, national education, samitis, Town Hall, Calcutta 1906

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the phases of leadership in the Swadeshi Movement?
o: The movement had no identifiable Moderate phase
The Moderate phase began only after 1906, while Extremist control ended in 1905
The Moderate phase involved petitions, while Extremist control emerged from 1906
Both phases relied exclusively on armed rebellion from the beginning
accepted.x: The early Moderate phase was associated with petition-based politics under leaders such as S.N. Banerjea, K.K. Mitra and Prithwishchandra Ray; Extremist control emerged from 1906.
accepted.tq: Compare the methods and chronology of the two phases instead of matching names alone.
accepted.sec: Techniques and programme - boycott, national education, samitis, Town Hall, Calcutta 1906

accepted.s: Which one of the following regional associations is correctly matched?
o: Bengal — Aurobindo Ghosh, Bipin Chandra Pal and Ashwini Kumar Dutt
Punjab — V.O. Chidambaram Pillai and Ajit Singh
Madras — Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Syed Haider Raza
Delhi — Konda Venkatappayya and C.Y. Chintamani
accepted.x: Aurobindo Ghosh, Bipin Chandra Pal and Ashwini Kumar Dutt were associated with Bengal. The other options combine leaders from different regions.
accepted.tq: Start with the complete regional cluster and reject cross-regional substitutions.
accepted.sec: Leaders → region

accepted.s: Who led the Swadeshi activities in Delhi?
accepted.x: Syed Haider Raza was identified with the Swadeshi movement in Delhi.
accepted.tq: Use the region–leader pairing rather than the more familiar Punjab and Madras names.
accepted.sec: Leaders → region

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with Andhra?
accepted.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was associated with Vijayawada. Gadicherla was associated with Bandar, Konda Venkatappayya with Guntur, and C.Y. Chintamani with Vizag.
accepted.tq: Use the place–leader pairs to catch the deliberate swapping of Andhra centres.
accepted.sec: Leaders → region

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Chilakamarti was associated with Rajahmundry. The other regional associations are Gadicherla–Bandar, Konda Venkatappayya–Guntur and Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao–Vijayawada.
accepted.tq: Check the repeated Andhra locations carefully and identify the non-swapped pair.
accepted.sec: Leaders → region
